name: dirac
desc: General-purpose video codec aimed at a range of resolutions
why: A BBC wavelet-based video codec is a fascinating alternative design, but it is old, obscure, and possibly stale.

brief.what_it_is: Dirac is a general-purpose video codec, according to its SourceForge page, aimed at resolutions from QCIF (176x144) to HDTV (1920x1080), progressive or interlaced. The listed executables suggest the input is raw or uncompressed video and still-image formats, such as RGB, YUV variants, UYVY and BMP, and the output is a compressed Dirac stream, which dirac_decoder reverses. Those input and output formats are inferred from executable names only, not from documentation I read. The package also includes a Perl test-file generator and an instrumentation tool.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage gives only a short framing: it is meant to cover a wide range of resolutions and to be competitive with other state-of-the-art codecs. I did not find a longer statement of purpose.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage says Dirac uses wavelets, motion compensation and arithmetic coding. I did not read a README or design document that explains the pipeline in more detail.
brief.install_notes: No install or build instructions were retrieved. The SourceForge page lists Linux, Windows and BSD as operating systems and C++ as the programming language. The download button was present, but I did not follow it to a files page or archive.
brief.standout: Most mainstream codecs are DCT block-based, so a wavelet-plus-motion-compensation design with arithmetic coding is an unusual choice. The bundled colour-conversion tools (RGBtoYUV420, UYVYtoYUV422 and similar) also make the package feel like a standalone test-bench toolchain. The scout note calls it a BBC design, but the homepage does not say that, so treat the BBC attribution as unverified.
brief.status: quiet. The SourceForge page shows Last Update 2013-06-04, a registration date of 2004-02-18, and a 4.8 rating from 19 reviews, with the most recent review from 2015. I found no newer release or commit information.
brief.caveats: The official 'Dirac Web Site' link on SourceForge did not give a usable URL, and diracvideo.org now serves unrelated gambling spam, so I could not reach the project's own site. I read no README, docs or source, so there are no build steps, licence details beyond the SourceForge listing, or limitations beyond what is listed here. The SourceForge page lists three licences (GPLv2, LGPLv2 and MPL 1.1), which may need checking against the source. One 2015 user review says common players (MPC-HC, FFplay, SMplayer, MediaInfo) do not recognise the *.rgb test videos.
quotes: Dirac is a general-purpose video codec aimed at resolutions from QCIF (176x144) to HDTV (1920x1080) progressive or interlaced.
It uses wavelets, motion compensation and arithmetic coding and aims to be competitive with other state of the art codecs.
